# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 5 (Bi-Vb Pc5)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc5
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 5
**Title (English, from literature):** Intimate washing
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Udakasuddhika Sikkhāpada* ("Intimate washing") is the fifth expiation (*pācittiya*) rule in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* of the Vinaya Piṭaka. It stipulates that a nun commits an offense requiring confession if she inserts more than two joints of the fingers into the vagina when washing or cleansing herself with water [Hüsken 1997; Hirakawa 1982]. According to the origin narrative, Mahāpajāpatī Gautamī reported to the Buddha that the nuns suffered from unpleasant body odor in their pubic area, whereupon the Buddha allowed intimate washing with water (*udakasuddhi*) but set strict anatomical limits on finger insertion [Hüsken 1997; Hirakawa 1982]. Scholars have observed that this narrative is one of only two places in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (alongside Saṅghādisesa 8) where a nun communicates directly with the Buddha rather than relying on monks as intermediaries, and that the rule directly resolves doubts arising from the preceding rules (Pācittiyas 3 and 4) which prohibit inserting or striking with foreign objects [Hüsken 1997].

Curated parallels exist across the Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga traditions of nearly all early Buddhist schools, including the Theravāda *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* and *Parivāra* (both Pc 5), the Dharmaguptaka (Pc 72), Mahīśāsaka (Pc 73), Sarvāstivāda (Pc 72 / Pc 74), and Mūlasarvāstivāda versions preserved in Chinese (Pc 75) and Tibetan (*xct-mu-bi-vb-pc95*), as well as corresponding rules in the Mahāsāṃghika tradition [Hirakawa 1982]. DharmaNexus corroborates alignment with the Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records over 400 shared formulaic passages across 100 texts, showing its densest textual overlap with the Khandhaka texts (such as Kd 6, Kd 1, Kd 20, Kd 15, and Kd 8) and other *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* rules (including Ss 3, Pc 3, Pc 6, Pc 15, Pc 24, Pc 30, and Pc 96) [DharmaNexus].
